Agent-first interface to Galley (the local agent team orchestrator).

Usage: galley [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  sessions  Operations on multiple sessions (list / search)
  session   Operations on a single session (brief / show / follow / write)
  status    Aggregate counts (total / running / waitingInput / errored) plus a `live` busy/queued rollup when Galley Core is reachable
  health    Run local health probes. Python-dependent rows report the legacy value `deferred_b4`, meaning "not probed by this command"
  version   Print the CLI + schema version
  project   Project operations (create / list / brief / show / follow / update / pin / unpin / archive-sessions / delete). `delete` is destructive: child sessions detach to ungrouped and survive. `archive-sessions` archives the conversations and keeps the project; there is no archive of the project itself
  llm       LLM commands. `llm list` prints the model list of the current runtime (Galley model store for managed, the GUI's warmup cache for external GA). `llm set` persists a per-session pick and tells any live runner. `llm set-default` changes the managed default model
  schedule  Scheduled tasks: one-off or repeating, that start a session or wake the assistant (the main chat). `list` / `show` read SQLite directly; the writes go through Galley Core. `delete` cancels: the task stays readable with `cancelledAt`
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --schema <N>  Pin the schema version this caller expects. Current binaries speak `3` and still accept `1` and `2` for every command that survived unchanged. A mismatch exits 2 (`invalid_args`) with a message prefixed `schema_mismatch:`. Omit to use the binary's default (currently `3`)
  -h, --help        Print help
  -V, --version     Print version

session:
Operations on a single session (brief / show / follow / write)

Usage: galley session [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  brief    One-row summary for a session id, plus a `live` run-state object (`busy` / `openRun` / `queuedCount` …) when Galley Core is reachable
  show     Conversation messages for a session, oldest first. Without a window flag: the full transcript (or its last `--tail` messages)
  send     Send a user message into a session. Persists the message with the supplied origin and dispatches it to the live runner; a mid-run send is held in Galley Core's queue (`dispatch: "queued"`) and runs when the current task finishes. While the agent waits on an `ask_user` question (`live.askPending`), a send is the answer and dispatches at once, ahead of queued messages. Requires Galley Core (exit 4 if the socket isn't reachable)
  watch    Stream live runner events from a session. NDJSON on stdout, one event per line, no backlog. Exits cleanly when the runner exits (`{"stream":"end",...}`) or on SIGINT; exit 3 when the session has no live runner — prefer `follow` unless you need raw events
  follow   Read the recent transcript, then follow live runner events if a runner is available. Unlike `watch`, this command gracefully ends when there is no live runner
  wait     Poll persisted session state until an agent-visible message appears (with `--until-idle`, and the run has ended) or the bounded wait times out. Intended for Supervisor / IM flows where a local tool timeout must not be treated as task failure
  new      Create a new session with a first user message. Atomic: session row + first message commit together or roll back together. Returns `{session, message, dispatch}` with `dispatch=dispatched` after Galley Core starts a runner and sends the first task. Runner start/send failures exit 5 so callers know delegation did not begin
  btw      Send a transient "by the way" side question into a running session. The runner answers it inline without disturbing the main task. Not persisted to the transcript; requires a live runner (exit 5 otherwise)
  stop     Stop the current turn in a session. Aborts the running task but keeps the runner alive, so a later `session send` resumes without a respawn. Reversible in effect. Idempotent: stopping an idle session returns `{dispatch: "already_stopped"}` and exit 0
  archive  Archive a session — flips status to `archived` and hides it from the GUI sidebar's active list. Reversible via `session restore`
  restore  Restore (unarchive) a previously archived session. Flips status from `archived` back to `idle`; no-op if the session wasn't archived
  move     Move a session into / out of a project. `--to=<project-id>` attaches; omit `--to` to detach (move to ungrouped)
  rename   Rename a session, as the desktop does: the title stays, the auto title no longer replaces it. An empty title gives it back to Galley. The main chat cannot be renamed (`main_chat_protected:`, exit 2)
  pin      Pin a session to the top of the desktop's list. An archived session cannot be pinned (exit 2), nor the main chat (`main_chat_protected:`)
  unpin    Unpin a session
  delete   Permanently delete a session: its messages and attachments go too, and nothing brings it back (`session archive` is the reversible one). A live runner is shut down first. The main chat cannot be deleted (`main_chat_protected:`, exit 2)
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --schema <N>  Pin the schema version this caller expects. Current binaries speak `3` and still accept `1` and `2` for every command that survived unchanged. A mismatch exits 2 (`invalid_args`) with a message prefixed `schema_mismatch:`. Omit to use the binary's default (currently `3`)
  -h, --help        Print help

Poll persisted session state until an agent-visible message appears (with `--until-idle`, and the run has ended) or the bounded wait times out. Intended for Supervisor / IM flows where a local tool timeout must not be treated as task failure

Usage: galley session wait [OPTIONS] <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>  Session id

Options:
      --schema <N>                 Pin the schema version this caller expects. Current binaries speak `3` and still accept `1` and `2` for every command that survived unchanged. A mismatch exits 2 (`invalid_args`) with a message prefixed `schema_mismatch:`. Omit to use the binary's default (currently `3`)
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>          Maximum wait time in seconds [default: 300]
      --poll <POLL>                Poll interval in seconds. Values below 1 are clamped to 1 [default: 5]
      --tail <TAIL>                Return only the last N messages in wait snapshots [default: 20]
      --final-show [<FINAL_SHOW>]  Include final tail messages in the final payload. Defaults true; pass `--final-show=false` for a compact final row [default: true] [possible values: true, false]
      --after-turn <AFTER_TURN>    Only count agent messages with turnIndex >= N as completion. Guards multi-turn sessions: without it, send→wait returns immediately on the PREVIOUS turn's answer
      --until-idle                 Complete only when the run has also ended. Without this flag any agent message with content (past `--after-turn`) completes the wait, and every intermediate step has content, so a long run returns on a progress step. With it, completion also needs Galley Core to report no run open or in progress (`live.openRun` and `live.agentRunning` both false). A pending ask_user question counts as ended: read `live.askPending` from the final frame's `session` and the question from the asking row's `askUser`. Queued messages keep the run open, so the wait lasts until they have all run. A run seen ended is confirmed by a second read 1s later (so the last row can land) before the wait completes from that read. On a poll where Core is unreachable, the output condition alone decides, with no pause

schedule:

  show     One task, cancelled or not. Read-only — opens SQLite directly
  create   Create a task. Give exactly one of `--at` (a one-off) and `--daily` / `--weekly` / `--monthly` (with `--time`)

  delete   Cancel a task (a soft delete): it never fires again and leaves the default list; `show` and `list --all` still read it
  enable   Turn a task back on
  disable  Pause a task
